answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token deposit before submitting jobs, then slash it when audits prove fabricated results. Auditors are bonded agents, and successful challengers receive part of the penalty. A plume of fake identities therefore costs capital per identity and risks forfeiture; splitting funds thinly also limits each agent’s influence. The saffron inlet on an audit dashboard is only decoration: security comes from collateral and enforceable penalties.
